correctness.rationale: For the unique unit-sphere maximal-volume nine-vertex 4-polytope, the square and pentagon occupy orthogonal 2-planes. Splitting the augmented 5×5 affine determinant gives area(square triple)·|det(pentagon pair)|/12 and |det(square pair)|·area(pentagon triple)/12. The 3+2, 2+3 and degenerate splits contribute 20 of each of four positive levels and 46 zero subsets; their sum is C(9,5)=126. Divide by Medgyes V=5sin(2π/5)/6, use sin(π/5)/sin(2π/5)=(√5−1)/2 and compare strict levels. Exactly 4 adjacent square pairs times 5 pentagon (1,2,2)-gap triples maximize, and successive separate-affine vertex replacement proves equality of the unrestricted contained-simplex maximum (not classification of all maximizers). Direct independent 126-determinant computation gave [46,20,20,20,20] and 20 maxima. The theorem is about this unique free sum, not all nine-vertex polytopes.
